text: Eighteen lessons ago, a six-week data access request reached the board. This lesson closes that story and looks back on everything built since.

LTV Global went from an ungoverned landscape to a governed program: five CDEs with owners, SQL quality checks, lineage and a golden record, access and retention policy, KPIs and a workflow, a permanent operating model, an AI governance strategy, a target architecture, and a board-ready presentation.

First caveat: time. Eighteen lessons read as one continuous sprint. A real version of this program plays out over twelve to twenty-four months, across multiple budget cycles, defended more than once along the way.

Second caveat: politics. This capstone's decisions landed cleanly in one meeting each. In practice, a domain owner who loses an authoritative-source call often pushes back, and the operating model only holds together with real executive backing when that happens.

Third caveat: iteration. DateOfBirth surfacing mid-program and the drift Lesson 15's consistency check caught weren't edge cases — they're what a real governance program looks like. Finding zero gaps isn't maturity; it's not looking hard enough.

This program is never frozen at Lesson 18 — the operating model keeps producing and correcting all of it going forward. And everything built here is now a portfolio you can walk a hiring manager through, which is exactly where this course goes next.
The capstone is complete. Lesson 19 opens Chapter Two: Data Governance Career Paths and Roles.
